rationale:
ROUND 3, responding to the 2026-08-24 10:52 REVISE (gating objection from bug_historian). What changed since round 2 is the one thing that round could not supply: THE OWNER HAS RULED (2026-08-24) that the root-behaviour fix the seat demanded is built NOW, folded into one change — the occurrence derivation (RFC_032 §9c) AND the detector/seam empty-id work. It is no longer 'deferred to an RFC': the initial implementation plan exists at bugfix_283_component_instance_scope/PLAN_2026-08-24_occurrence_derivation_and_empty_id_detector.md and RFC_032 §10 records the ruling. The plan does what the seat's objection asked: id="" becomes its own detector class (not a widened reElementID — one empty id is already a defect, and empty-vs-duplicate are different diagnoses); the render-time fail-loud arms the Error log that ALREADY exists at component_library.go:1103-1110, refusal-direction, conditional on a measured-zero log census per the 2026-08-02 §2 authority ruling; and every DetectInstanceCollisions caller's behaviour change is enumerated in a table. That work is a separate reviewed change with its own council round — THIS round's scope stays the retirement as committed and live.

THE SEAT'S MISSING CHECK IS RUN, AND IT WAS RIGHT TO DEMAND IT. Formal corpus-wide census (LIKE '%id=""%' over non-removed page_components.rendered_html, not my earlier ad-hoc grep): **6 rows on 6 pages across 2 sites (as of 2026-08-24)** — the 4 idea.uk guide pages I had found, PLUS 2 dartsonline.com pages (/brands/, /shop/) I had NOT. And the extra two are a THIRD cause: category-listing declares id="{{.category_slug}}" — a CONTENT field, nothing to do with the retired placeholder — which rendered empty. This vindicates the seat's core thesis (any unbound field in an id attribute produces the class; call-site patches cannot close it) and is exactly why the owner-ruled fix makes the fail-loud general rather than ComponentID-specific. The seat's related point that my census methodology had already under-counted once (the is_active filter missing 2 of 3 rows) is conceded and logged in WRONG_CALLS; both misses shared a shape — a filter narrowing the question without narrowing the claim.

THE FOUR IDEA.UK CASUALTIES ARE OWNED: owner ruling 2026-08-24, repaired on their lane even at the cost of content generation — CONTRIB filed in idea_uk_section_data_missing/ with the measured state (their content_data is intact, so a correctly-shaped rerender likely suffices; the cheap step is ordered first and the trap that made the last rerender a silent no-op is named). The dartsonline pair routes through the ruled detector work, since its cause is the general class.

EDITQUALITY'S PROCESS OBJECTION IS TAKEN: round 2's 'edit 3' was a verification SELECT dressed as an edit. This round has no such edit — the ledger recordings (247/250 via the runner's own --record-only, artifact-checked first) are evidence, cited in grounded_in where evidence lives.

THE THIRD BINDING (v3_site_actions.go:2385) REMAINS DEFERRED, and the reason strengthened overnight: the file gained ANOTHER session's uncommitted hunk (the 345 lane's ladder call-site) — the second occupant in two days — and my own uncommitted deletion of the binding was OVERWRITTEN by a concurrent session on the night of 08-23. Committing that file today mints a passenger, the exact failure this correlation's round 1 was vetoed over. The binding is inert (census 2026-08-24: 0 templates spell the placeholder; both live render paths that USED the retired key no longer bind it) and the exact edit is staged in the lane NOTES §15 for the first session that finds the file clean. bug_historian's reactivation concern is real and is answered by the ruled work, not by this round: once the fail-loud ships, a reactivated unconverted template REFUSES to render rather than serving id="".

edits.sketch:
commit 024303681771db43f2315055cfc4537f250c8388
Author: cqls <aaa@designconsultancy.co.uk>
Date:   Sun Aug 23 18:56:55 2026 +0100

    RFC_032 step 3: retire the ComponentID bindings - two of three deleted, the third named rather than committed because its file would break HEAD
    
    Owner ruling RFC_032 section 8 is converge on InstanceID and retire
    ComponentID. Step 2 converted the templates this morning; this is the
    retirement.
    
    THE ORDER IS THE WHOLE RISK. The renderer runs missingkey=zero, so a
    placeholder with no binding does not error - it renders EMPTY. A template
    still spelling id="{{.ComponentID}}" after this change renders id="", and the
    collision detector cannot see that: reElementID is \sid="([^"{}]+)" and the +
    requires at least one character. Deleting too early produces an invalid page
    that every automated check calls clean. Not hypothetical: four idea.uk guide
    pages serve <section id=""> today, and I fetched one to confirm it.
    
    So the precondition is zero and it is measured, not assumed. A census over
    EVERY live table with a template-or-html column - a DO block over
    information_schema rather than a guess at which table matters - found the
    placeholder in exactly two places: component_versions (history, which is its
    job) and content_components, which held THREE rows, not the one an
    is_active-filtered query had shown me earlier. pricing was active with no
    placements; header and footer were inactive with none, same 2025-11-21 library
    seed. All three are now converted and the count is 0.
    
    Those three could not go through the pipeline for a structural reason worth
    recording: the conversion files one work item per component, site_work_items
    .site_id is NOT NULL, and a template's site is only reachable through the
    pages that place it. Zero placements means no honest site, so the
    placement-driven seed skips them silently. They were converted by the real
    converter and passed the real gate, each with a control proving the gate
    REFUSES the unconverted original; only the persistence is by hand, mirroring
    writeScopedTemplate and guarded so a re-run is a no-op. The two inactive rows
    were done deliberately - they cannot render today, but after this change a
    reactivated row is exactly the invisible-empty-id case.
    
    The two seed files are part of the same hole. Both create their component with
    the placeholder, both carry ON CONFLICT (name) DO UPDATE, and neither is
    recorded in schema_migrations - so the runner's own pending test treats them
    as pending and a migration run would overwrite two templates converted this
    morning. One line changed in each, the id, so no other replay hazard those
    files carry is widened by me.
    
    WHAT IS NOT HERE. The third binding, v3_site_actions.go:2385, is edited in the
    working tree and deliberately NOT committed. That file carries another
    session's uncommitted work - five further hunks calling three functions in
    section_metadata_keys.go, which is UNTRACKED and absent from HEAD. Committing
    it by pathspec would take their half-finished work with mine and put calls to
    undefined symbols on the shared branch, breaking the build for every session.
    It is inert to leave: with zero templates referencing the placeholder, a
    binding nothing reads changes no output. Named here, in the lane NOTES and in
    RFC_032 so it is finished rather than forgotten.
    
    Full actions suite green, built and tested from a clean git archive HEAD
    extract taken AFTER HEAD moved - the first extract was stale and its failure
    is what surfaced the other session's WIP in the first place.
    
    Council-Submitted: e8c7414c-426d-4aee-a0ca-3e2e2400cbec

plan.risks:
1) A reviewer must judge whether an owner-ruled, plan-committed build ANSWERS the gating objection or merely re-schedules it. The honest statement: the root fix is not yet code. What exists is a ruling, a plan with measured inputs, and a named building thread. If the council's bar is 'code or nothing', this round fails that bar and should say so plainly rather than approve.

2) The third binding stays live until the contested file clears. Mitigations are real but indirect: nothing binds the retired key on the two paths that render the RFC_032 templates; the ruled fail-loud will refuse a reactivated unconverted template; and the exact edit is staged. A reviewer who weighs an inert binding as heavier than a passenger risk should object here.

3) The census fixed the COUNT but not the METHODOLOGY class: both of my under-counts came from filters narrowing the question without narrowing the claim. The formal query is now stated inline so a reviewer can re-run it rather than trust it.

4) Nothing in this round changes running behaviour — both deletions have been live since v1.0.1332. This is the record converging on what production already is, which is this estate's stated review-after-the-fact design (owner ruling 2026-07-29 §2).
